PREAMBLE:
l. Agriculture is a profession on which the highest percentage of the
population of the State is directly and indirectly depends for its eaming.
Whereas in the past 20 years or so, there has been significant
enhancement in the production and productivity of crops, but the income

of the farmer has not grown proportionately. Not only that, the vagaries
of weather too has been impacting agriculture and farm income
considerably. It is high tirne that farming be so modified, so that the farm
income be optimised by utilising all resources and potential available in
the farm sector in an integrated manner.
2. With these in view, the Govemment of India gave a call for doubling of
farmer's income of 2014-15 by 2A22-23. Both, the Govemment of India
as well as the Govemment of Karnataka, took measures and drew up an
action plan to achieve this target. The State Action Plan focussed on
popularising Integrated Farming System (IFS) in each agro-climatic zone
with providing better markets and market intelligence as the means to
achieve the goal.
3. In the rneeting of 25.08.2021 chaired by the Hon'ble Chief Minister, he
has stressed the point of concentrating on Secondary Agriculture as the
means to taking agriculture forward and achieving the goal of doubling of
farmer's inconre. For this, he directed that a Directorate of Secondary

"Report of the Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income" prepared by the
Cornmittee on Doubling Farmers' Income, Department of Agriculture,
Cooperation and Farmers' Welfare, is an enterprise that has direct
involvement of the agricultural community and must provide groMh
opportunity to the primary sector. Secondary level activities, linked to
agriculture, can include economic activities from the secondary or the
tertiary sectors.
Therefore, secondary agriculture a productive activity at enterprise

level that-
i. utilizes as raw material the primary product and by-products of
agriculture and other biological resources available locally in its rural
agrarian neighbourhood; and/or
ii. deploys locally available skills or a high level of rural manpower to
operate/manage/ maintain the production ofgoods and services; and
iii. promotes farm/cottage and village level rural industries by utilizing
low intensity of capital and technology.
Secondary Agriculture includes food and non-food bio-resource
based products for human and industrial use.

blocks.text: Preparation of Secondary Asriculture Action Ptan
A. Each Head of the related Department shall constitute a working
group/cell of up to five persons, including one who would be from the
faculty of the University which deals with the subject of the department,
one a person who is an experr in analysis of the data available in the field
of the department, one who is proficient in project formulation and one
who is from the an expert on the subject but is not from the govemment
sector.
B. A working group/cell of each department shall identifli and set annual
targets up to district level in the field of secondary Agriculture consistent
with the availability of funds, and prepare a project/action plan of their
department along with where and how they expect convergence with
other departments. Integrated Farming System, forward and backward
linkages, value addition, packing, branding, FpO formation, providing
avenues of sale so that better prices are obtained by the farmers for their
produce and promotion of rural/cottage industries shall be considered,
examined and covered in the project/action plan of each department. This
shall be submitted to the Head of the Department (HoD).
C. The concerned HoDs would consider and finalize these targets and
submit it to the Director of Secondary Agriculture who will get compiled
the project/action plan district-wise, department-wise and for the State
would submit the composite project/ action plan for the approval of the
SLSC. After approval of the SLSC the approved project/action plan of
secondary agriculture along with the plans of each department will be

taken up for implementation. The project/action plan will be implemented
by the District Level Implementation Committee for Secondary
Agriculture.

blocks.text: Roles and Resoonsibilities of the DLICSA
( 1) To coordinate with various departments concemed with skill

development, promotion of cottage and village industries, financial
institutions, training organisations, research institutes etc., and
facilitate primary and secondary processing activities.
(2) To prepare comprehensive district plans for promotion of secondary
agriculture based on local resources.
(3) To promote aggregation platforms where the raw produce can be
aggregated and fed to village level industries.
(4) To monitor and review the progress of implementation of the plan as
frequently as possible, not later than once in every month.
(5) To take measures for co-ordination among implementing departments and

timely convergence, particularly in implementing of IFS and realization
of forward and backward linkages.

The DLICSA may co-opt more members and or NGOs for effective and
timely implementation of the plan.

There shall be no additional post created for the SLSC and DLICSA or
any of its bodies, Working Groups etc., nor any permanent/temporary additional
infrastructure created or any vehicle purchased or taken on outsource basis.
